al_barn_area.blurb: The Barn Area is one of the main clusters of sandstone boulders at Hospital Boulders, on the west brow of Lookout Mountain just north of Gadsden. It sits close to the parking lot, so the walk in is short and easy, and it makes a natural first stop. The problems are all bouldering, with most falling between V1 and V5 and a small group of harder lines from V6 up to V10. Desperado, Vertical Cartography and Don't Look Back are among the best known. The property is climber-owned and open only from dawn to dusk, with no camping, so plan your day around the gate.

al_eddie_area.blurb: The Eddie Area is a dense pocket of sandstone boulders at Hospital Boulders, just north of Gadsden on the west brow of Lookout Mountain. It is a short, easy hike from the parking lot, and it has a wider spread of difficulty than most neighboring sectors: plenty of V0 to V4 problems for warming up, a solid group of V5 to V8 lines, and a few of the hardest problems on the property, including Hustle and Flow and Mega Man. Mystified and No Parking on the Dance Floor are popular mid-grade tests. There are no restrooms on site, so pack out waste, and stay on established trails.

al_lower_area.blurb: The Lower Area is part of the sandstone boulder field at Hospital Boulders, on the west brow of Lookout Mountain just north of Gadsden. Its problems lean toward the moderate end: most fall between V2 and V5, with a few easier warm-ups and only a handful above V6. Hero, Scarecrow and Pittman Arete are among the favorites here. The whole property is a short, easy walk from the parking lot, is climber-owned, and is open from dawn to dusk only. Camping is not allowed, dogs must be leashed, and the gate should be locked behind you.
al_lower_area.parking_note: Park in the gated lot at the end of Scenic Highway, just past the hospital off I-59 north of Gadsden. A short owner-built road leads to the lot, which is under a minute on foot from the boulder field. Park only in the marked spaces and lock the gate behind you.

al_right_side_cliff.blurb: The Right Side Cliff is the portion of Yellow Bluff that is open to climbers, outside Huntsville. It is a sandstone cliff with a blend of sport and trad lines, ranging from easy routes to a handful in the 5.13 range, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.12. Lucifer's Revenge is a popular 5.9, while Orange Crush, Tilt-a-Whirl and Novacaine span the mid grades to the hard end. The land around the cliff is private: do not top out, keep voices down, and turn back where the climber-owned stretch ends at a no-trespassing sign. Camping is not allowed, and the footing near the rim and the base can be loose and slippery.
al_right_side_cliff.approach: A trail leads to the right-hand end of the cliff. From there the routes spread leftward along the base for roughly 1,500 feet, to the end of the climber-owned land marked by a no-trespassing sign.

al_palisades_park.blurb: Palisades Park is a Blount County park near Oneonta, north of Birmingham, with a low sandstone cliff line just below the parking area. The rock runs from roughly 30 to 80 feet and the climbing is mostly traditional and top-rope, with the bulk of routes between 5.7 and 5.10 and a few harder lines. It is a popular first outdoor crag, since most routes are easy to rig as top-ropes from above, though the grades can feel stiff and some cracks are serious for new leaders. There are no bolted sport lines. Camping is not allowed, and trees should be padded when rigging.
al_palisades_park.parking_note: Drive to the county park outside Oneonta and use the main park lot; the cliff line begins just below it. Follow the signs on the county roads from US 231 north of town.
al_palisades_park.approach: Walk from the lot to the top of the cliff near the picnic pavilion, then scramble down a fourth-class gully or chimney to the base of the routes.

al_sun_wall.blurb: The Sun Wall is one of the main cliffs at Sand Rock, also called Cherokee Rock Village, a county park near Leesburg on the southern end of Lookout Mountain. The rock is sandstone, and the wall carries mostly sport routes with a good number of trad lines and a lone top-rope. It leans toward the harder side of the park: the bulk of climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a strong showing at 5.12. Misty, Dreamscape, Rave and Dreamworld are the best-known lines. Sandstone here is generally solid but can lose holds, so avoid climbing right after rain. Walk-ins at the park are short.

al_grass_man_area.blurb: The Grass Man Area is a sector of sandstone boulders at Moss Rock Preserve in Hoover, a city park on the south side of Birmingham. The rock has coarse, grippy texture that rewards technical face climbing and steep moves. Problems here are all bouldering, mostly between V0 and V7 with a few harder lines, including Serenity Now, Road to Nowhere and Eyeflies. Well-marked trails lead from the trailhead to the boulders. Cooler fall and winter days give the best friction. The preserve is open sunrise to sunset, with no camping or fires, and pets must be leashed. Stay on trail to protect the native plants.
al_grass_man_area.parking_note: Use the preserve's public lot next to the kiosk and trailhead, and leave before the posted closing time. Park only in the designated lots.

al_rainbow_mountain.blurb: Rainbow Mountain is a small city preserve in Madison, just outside Huntsville, where climbing has been officially welcomed in recent years. The bouldering is short, close to the car, and friendly: most problems fall between V0 and V3, which makes it a good place for beginners or an after-work session. The preserve also has a pavilion, a playground and several miles of trails. It is open from dawn to dusk, and camping, fires and slacklining are not allowed. Stay off the trails for a day after rain, and expect the smaller lot to fill on busy days.
al_rainbow_mountain.parking_note: Two lots serve the preserve: the main one beside the pavilion and kiosk, and a smaller uphill lot by the water tower that is closest to the boulders. When the lots fill, the preserve closes to new visitors, so carpool and do not park on the street.
al_rainbow_mountain.approach: The walk from the uphill lot to the boulders is short.
